Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL G0VERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II, EDSA cor. Mapagmahal St. Diliman, Quezon City OFFIæ OF 200b 14 May 2008 VICE GOVERNOR EDWARD THOMAS F. JOSON Provincial Capitol Building Cabanatuan City Dear Vice Governor Joson: This refers to your letter requesting for a legal opinion regarding DILG Opinion No. 11, series of 2008, dated 17 March 2008 vis-å-vis the additional facts and Supreme Court decisions you presented in the instant letter. It may be recalled that in said DILG Opinion No. II, this Department opined that the series of memoranda you issued as Acting Governor could well fall within the meaning and contemplation of the word "appoint" found under Section 46 (a) of the Local Government Code since it directed certain officials other than those officials earlier designated by Governor Umali to perform the functions of certain offices. Such being the case and per the limitations on the power of the Acting Governor under Section 46 (a) of the Local Government Code, the subject series of memoranda should have only been issued by the Acting Governor at the time when the temporary incapacity of the Governor shall have already exceed thirty (30) working days. In your instant letter, you informed the Department of the following additional facts leading to your issuance of the series of memoranda subject matter of the abovesaid DILG Opinion No. 11, to wit: 1. "On July 18, 2008 and subsequent dates thereafter, Governor Aurelio Umali issued several special orders designating different department heads and regular employees to assume positions outside and irrelevant to their existing appointments. 2. In relation thereto, special orders were likewise issued designating employees from different

-2 departments with lower rank to assume the above- stated positions as Officers in charge. It is also worthy to mention that the persons who were assigned as officers in charge lack the required competency, qualifications and experience relative to the positions they were ordered to hold. 3. The personnel involved in memorandum 02-21, s. 2008 are heads of offices and regular employees who were designated by Governor Aurelio Umali to assume functions irrelevant and totally inconsistent with their original appointments. 4. The above-mentioned department heads (who are ho Iding career positions) and other regular employees affected were all "assigned" in the Provincial Information Office and other offices citing the reason "for exigency of the service" without securing their respective consents. 5. These department and office heads were all foiced to report at the Provincial Information Officer (PIO) doing nothing during the entire office hours and they were made under the supervision of Mr. Edgardo Rilton whose appointment was disapproved by the Civil Service Commission due to Zack of civil service eligibility. 6. These personnel, who were victims of this unlawful assignments, had made clear their grievance and objections to these unlawful transfer constituting their demotions from their respective offices and are in the process of preparing and filing the necessary complaints with the appropriate government agencies. 7. The undersigned is weZZ aware of the ruling made by the Supreme Court in the case of Divinagracia, Jr. vs. Sto. Tomas, 244 SCRA 595, that a transfer that results in promotion or demotion, advancement or reduction or transfer that aims to hire the employee away from his permanent position, cannot be done without the emp loyees consent, the unconsented

-3- transfer amounts to removal. 8. Thus, on March 14, 2008, the undersigned issued the subject memoranda not to "appoint" the personnel stated therein but to order them to assume their respective positions as stated in their original appointments. Thus, anchoring on the Supreme Court pronouncement in Borromeo vs. Mariano (41 Phil. 322) and the foregoing antecedent facts, it is now your position that the series of memoranda you earlier issued is not an "appointment" contemplated in the Borromeo case but merely an order requiring the personnel who were previously lawfully appointed to exercise the functions of their respective offices and to assume their positions as such. It is further your conclusion that the issuance of the series of memoranda can neither be considered an appointment nor designation but merely an order for the respective employees and heads of offices to assume their offices pursuant to their original appointments. Hence, your instant request. In reply thereto, at the outset, may we emphasize that DILG Opinion No. 11, s. 2008, was issued in the light, context and perspective on the limitation of the Acting Local Chief Executive to issue appointments unless the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. For emphasis, may we restate Section 46 (a) of the Local Government Code, to wit: "(a) When the governor, city or municipal mayor, or punong barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave or absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice-governor, city or municipal vice mayor, or the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the locat chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceed thirty (30) working days. " In withholding from the Acting Local Chief Executive certain powers among which is appointment to be exercised within thirty (30) working days from the temporary incapacity of the Local Chief Executive, Congress may not have provided for such limitation for nothing. To our mind, the legislative intent was for the Acting Governor not to disturb, for a certain period of only thirty (30) working

-4- days during the temporary incapacity of the Governor, the officials and employees in the provincial organizational structure upon whom the Governor reposed his trust and confidence to perform their specific tasks. While we see your point that the series of memoranda you issued were not per se appointment as legally defined by the Supreme Court cases you mentioned but merely orders requiring the personnel who were previously lawfully appointed to exercise the functions of their respective offices and to assume their positions as such based on their original appointments, we cannot lose sight of the fact, however, that the Govemor had already earlier exercised his power of management prerogative in reassigning and transferring certain officials and employees of the province. In the light of the legislative intent, the exercise by the Governor of his management prerogative, whether erroneous or not, should be respected by his temporary successor even for thirty (30) working days only as anyway, after the said period, the Acting Governor can now also exercise his own management prerogative in running the affairs of the provincial government while the Govemor is temporarily absent. Those Department heads and officials affected by the earlier exercise by the Governor of his management prerogative can vindicate their rights and raise its legality to the proper forum and not by the action of the Acting Governor within the period of limitation as this would run counter to the legislative intent of Congress in providing the limitation. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Acting Secretary Legal:43/La cc: Director Josefina Castilla-Go DILG Regional Office No. Ili San Fernando City, Pampanga
